images.title: Equal shares of one roti
images.purpose: Show that one roti cut into n equal shares gives a fractional unit of 1/n, and the unit gets smaller as n grows.
images.composition: Three equal round rotis in one row with wide even gaps, each with one label below it, and one short line centred under the row.
images.exact_structure: Three round rotis of exactly the same size in a row. Left: cut by straight lines from the centre into 3 equal pieces, one piece filled teal #0072B2. Middle: cut into 6 equal pieces, one piece filled teal #0072B2. Right: cut into 12 equal pieces, one piece filled teal #0072B2. All other pieces plain with thin dark outlines. One label under each roti and one line centred under the row. Exactly 3 rotis, 3 shaded pieces.

images.takeaway: One whole in more equal shares gives a smaller fractional unit.
images.description: Three same-size rotis cut into 3, 6 and 12 equal pieces, one piece of each shaded teal and labelled 1/3, 1/6 and 1/12; the shaded share shrinks as the number of shares grows.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the shaded piece in each roti and say its name, 1 over the number of equal pieces.

image_decisions.why: Three same-size rotis cut into more and more equal shares show the one idea the practice builds on.
